rationale: PINS A TRUE EXPLANATION, not merely a present one. A type parameter is a real Go declaration (spec, Type parameter declarations) but it is SCOPED to its function or type, so it is not a symbol — the same reading LocalsAreNotSymbols applies to locals. The lane still EMITS the reference and that is right: `Pair -> K` is a true fact (Pair uses its parameter K) and suppressing it would hide a real dependency. What was wrong is the EXPLANATION. With no type-parameter set to consult, those rows fell through to the generic declared-type code `declared_type_leaf_whose_declaring_file_is_out_of_scope`, which says the declaring file is outside this one — and for `K` that is FALSE, because its declaration is the `type_parameter_list` on the very same line. MEASURED on go-tools + terraform (3,422 files, 363,830 edges): 981 edges carried that false code; after the fix 0 do, and all 981 carry the new one. THE POINT OF THE NEW CODE IS THAT IT STATES TWO FACTS AT ONCE: the declaration IS in this file (`..._declared_here_...`, the half the old code got backwards) and it is scoped rather than package-level (`..._scoped_to_its_declaration_not_a_symbol`, the half that tells a consumer why no symbol exists to navigate to). A code that stated only one of those would be less wrong but still incomplete. THE CONTROL ROW IS WHAT MAKES THIS A FIX AND NOT A RELABEL: `Plain -> Missing` is a parameter-free reference to a type this file does not declare, so it must KEEP the generic out-of-scope code. A change that stamped the new code on every declared-type row would satisfy the positive rows while destroying the meaning of the old one, and this row would fail. THE FORBID ROW pins the absence direction: a `Generic -> T` row still claiming an out-of-scope declaring file is precisely the defect. NOT PINNED: the duplicate `Generic -> T` row (the signature mentions T twice; the emitter's source|target|relType key collapses them only when identical), and confidence/evidenceClass, which classifyEvidenceTier derives unchanged.

expectRelationships.comment: A generic function's own type parameter: the declaration is the type_parameter_list on this very line, so the out-of-scope code this row used to carry was false.
The second parameter of the same declaration, so the fix is not keyed to one letter.
A generic TYPE's parameter, reached from a struct FIELD rather than a signature — a different construction path, same explanation.

CONTROL: a parameter-free reference to a type this file DOES NOT declare must KEEP the generic out-of-scope code. If this row started claiming the type-parameter code, the change would be a relabel that destroyed the old code's meaning.

forbidRelationships.comment: THE DEFECT: a type-parameter reference still explained as an out-of-scope declaring file. The declaring file is this one.
The same lie on the struct-field path.
